newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram's party to shun India government.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram's party to shun India government.

text.p: Caretaker Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's regional party said on Sunday that it would not backtrack on a decision to stay out of a new centre-left government.

The leader of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), G.K. Moopanar, was asked if his party would reconsider its decision, announced late on Saturday, not to join a government led by prime minister-in-waiting Inder Kumar Gujral.
"No reconsideration," news agencies quoted Moopanar as saying.
Moopanar had been a leading contender to succeed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who resigned on April 11 after losing a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament.
But strong opposition from leftwing groups in Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front coalition as well as from his Janata Dal party dashed Moopanar's hopes.

The TMC's decision to stay out of the government while still supporting it could come as a blow to financial markets, which had been hoping that Chidambaram would survive the three-week spell of political turmoil.

Chidambaram was the architect of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget which delighted stock markets with its tax and tariff cuts, and investment incentives. He has been a strong advocate of liberal economic policies and an opponent of protectionism.

"Chidambaram's departure will send the wrong kind of signal to the rest of the world," Gautam Adhikari, former editor of the Times of India, told Reuters. "He had presented a face of India which is modern, progressive and open."
Gujral said there were "very good" chances that the TMC would reconsider its decision and join the government.
"We are absolutely confident that we will be able to persuade the TMC to participate in the new government," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Gujral as saying.

Newspapers speculated that Moopanar might be offered the post of deputy prime minister. Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu, convenor of the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee, said on Saturday that the alliance had not ruled out the creation of such a post.
But Moopanar said he was not interested. "I am not deputy prime minister material," PTI quoted him as saying.

Although the TMC said it would support a new government led by Gujral without taking any portfolios, its leaders did not attend a meeting on Sunday morning of United Front parliamentarians to elect Gujral as the chief.
Moopanar was quoted as saying his party had not learned of the meeting until it was too late to attend.

The TMC released a statement in the capital on Sunday saying it had decided to stay out of the new government because some sections of the United Front had "suspected its political morality and loyalty".
